head: In 1994, buying one CD online made the New York Times.
body: On 11 August 1994, a man in Philadelphia paid for a Sting CD with his card, over the internet. The Times ran it as news. Money on a public ledger is at that same moment right now.

head: Every new way to pay felt unsafe at first.
body: Typing your card into a website. Banking on your phone. Paying with a QR code. Each one went from "never" to "normal" because the rules got clearer and the tools got easier.

head: So what is on-chain finance? Plain English:
body: Your investments sit on a public ledger, in an account only you control. Every buy and sell leaves a receipt you can check yourself. And the market doesn't close at 4pm.

head: How to start without feeling like a dummy.
list: Learn first, then put money in.
Start with an amount you'd be fine losing.
Use an account only you control.
Check the receipts, not the promises.
body: The catch: it's newer tech, prices move fast, and scams copy the real thing.

head: You were early to the internet once.
body: Follow @blok.capital for one plain-English idea a week on building a portfolio you can actually see. Comment "1994" with the first thing you ever bought online.
